edits.old:
Build a hierarchy of this social-media post's subjects, like a book's subject index. Begin by understanding the complete post before dividing it into subjects.

Resolve each reference or local description to the complete supported description of its referent for that occurrence, using the whole post, including titles, enclosing headings, lists and shared predicates. Build complete specific subjects and expressed combinations from those resolved referents, retaining both enclosing relationships and local roles or purposes. Derive less specific descriptions only as broader headings. General knowledge may clarify language, identify referents, and recognize subjects, but every entity, modifier, action, and relationship in an entry must be stated or reasonably implied by the post.

Interpret names, labels, and hashtags by what they refer to; their component words alone do not establish a literal description. For an unresolved named subject, retain its name.

URLs and opaque encoded identifiers—including, but not limited to, Nostr public keys (`npub1…`), event IDs (`nevent1…`), and cryptographic hashes—provide no subject evidence. The surrounding prose may still establish subjects involving URLs or identifiers.

If ambiguity remains after understanding the complete post, give each supported interpretation its own directly stated subject, without uncertainty qualifiers. Co-mention or statement order alone does not establish relationships. Do not add commentary about plausibility or what is unclear or unstated.

For numbers in subject text, preserve what they refer to; any count or measurement interpretation and units must be supported by the post. Include calculated results only if explicitly stated.

Return only one JSON object with a `subjects` array containing the completed hierarchy. Present it broad-to-specific using section-style numbering (`1`, `1.1`, `1.1.1`), listing each heading before its subheadings. Return an object for each hierarchy entry with `number`, then `context`, then `subject`.

In `context`, identify the subject and the source context establishing its meaning. This may describe a particular instance supporting a general heading.

In `subject`, name the subject at that entry's level of generality. Keep details distinguishing a particular instance in its subheading, rather than importing them from `context` into the general heading. Each heading must be understandable without the post, its `context`, or other entries; it need not retell what the post says about the subject. Preserve the heading's meaning, negation, and relationships. For comparison entries, name both sides when provided. Make the wording concise.

Build a hierarchy of this social-media post's subjects, like a book's subject index. Understand the complete post before dividing it into subjects.

Resolve each reference or local description to the complete supported description of its referent for that occurrence, using the whole post, including titles, enclosing headings, lists and shared predicates. Before deriving broader headings, enumerate all specific subjects expressed literally, nonliterally or rhetorically by individual parts, combined parts or the whole post, even when unnamed. Retain individual subjects, particular instances and every expressed combination with their complete supported referents, amounts, modifiers, negation, enclosing relationships—including list membership—and local roles or purposes in `subject`; event descriptions do not replace the subjects involved. General knowledge may clarify language, identify referents and recognize subjects; every entity, modifier, action and relationship must be stated or reasonably implied by the post.

Interpret names, labels and hashtags by what they refer to; their component words alone do not establish literal descriptions. Retain the name of an unresolved named subject.

URLs and opaque encoded identifiers, including Nostr public keys (`npub1…`), event IDs (`nevent1…`) and cryptographic hashes, provide no subject evidence. Surrounding prose may establish subjects involving them.

If ambiguity remains after understanding the complete post, give every supported interpretation its own directly stated subject without uncertainty qualifiers. Co-mention or statement order alone does not establish relationships. Add no commentary about plausibility or what is unclear or unstated.

Preserve what numbers refer to; count or measurement interpretations and units must be supported by the post. Include calculated results only when explicitly stated.

Make each `subject` concise, understandable without the post, `context` or other entries, and faithful to its meaning, negation and relationships. Name both comparison sides when provided. A heading names its subject at its level of generality; it need not retell the post's assertion about it. Broader headings may omit instance details; complete source subjects retain those details in their own specific headings.

Derive broader headings by generalizing source meanings without adding restrictions. Judge each parent-child pair using only its `subject` strings across possible posts in any domain. The child itself must preserve every parent restriction: type, purpose, modifier, action, negation and relationship. If another post could fit the child but fail to fit the parent, broaden the parent or preserve the supported restriction in the child. A usual purpose does not restrict every instance; a purpose-qualified heading cannot contain an unrestricted item heading. The post's domain, `context` and other entries cannot supply a missing heading restriction.

Determine valid relationships before numbering, combine shared headings, and give every heading and subheading its own entry. For each complete source subject, compare its own wording with every returned heading using the parent check. An equal-meaning heading's own entry already represents the source subject; include it among the descendants of every more-general compatible heading, independently at every numbered occurrence even when surrounding branches differ. Placement elsewhere cannot repair a missing branch.

Return only one JSON object with a `subjects` array. Each entry has `number`, then `context`, then `subject`. Use section-style numbering (`1`, `1.1`, `1.1.1`), broad to specific, listing every heading before its subheadings. In `context`, identify the subject and the source establishing its meaning; this may describe a particular instance supporting a general heading.

edits.old:
For each enumerated subject, derive broader headings by generalizing its meaning without adding restrictions. An item's usual purpose is not a property of every instance: a purpose-qualified heading cannot contain an unrestricted item heading. Compare only the proposed `subject` strings across possible posts in any domain, including uses unlike the one described here. Classify what each heading necessarily means; the domain of this post cannot narrow an unrestricted heading. A child heading must itself preserve every restriction of its parent: type, purpose, modifier, action, negation and relationship. Imagine another post that fits the child heading: if it could fail to fit the proposed parent heading, broaden the parent or keep the supported restriction in the child wording. The post, `context` and other entries cannot supply a restriction missing from a heading.

Determine the valid relationships before numbering. For each enumerated complete source subject, use its own wording to find every returned heading whose parent check it passes. An equal-meaning heading's own entry already represents that source subject; place it among the descendants of every more-general compatible heading, independently for every numbered occurrence even when the surrounding branch differs. Combine shared headings and give every heading and subheading its own entry. Before returning JSON, check each completed parent-child pair using only its two heading strings; broaden the parent or preserve the supported restriction in the child if needed, while retaining the source subject. Read every source clause again: its specific referents, amounts, modifiers, negation and expressed relationships must still be present in subject headings, not only contexts. Finally, check every numbered parent occurrence for its complete collection of source subjects. A placement elsewhere cannot repair a missing branch.

With the post's meaning understood, first enumerate all specific subjects it expresses before deriving broader headings. Include subjects conveyed literally, nonliterally, or rhetorically by individual parts, multiple parts together, or the post as a whole, even when no phrase names them. Retain individual subjects, their particular instances and every expressed combination, with their complete supported referents, amounts, modifiers, negation and relationships in the subject strings; a description of an event does not replace the subjects involved.
